title: Binary Searchable Numbers in an Unsorted Array
summary: Analyze an algorithm similar to Binary Search on an unsorted array.
statement: Analyze an algorithm similar to Binary Search on an unsorted array. The function searches for a target value by repeatedly choosing a pivot. If the pivot matches the target, it returns true. If the pivot is less than the target, it removes the pivot and all elements to its left. If the pivot is greater, it removes the pivot and all elements to its right. The goal is to count how many target values are guaranteed to be found, regardless of the pivot selection, when the input array is unsorted.
constraints: nums has 1 through 100000 distinct integers from -100000 through 100000.
A target is guaranteed under arbitrary pivots exactly when every value left of it is smaller and every value right of it is larger.
reference_solution:
def count_binary_searchable_numbers(nums):
    size = len(nums)
    prefix = [float("-inf")] * size
    largest = float("-inf")
    for index in range(size):
        prefix[index] = largest
        largest = max(largest, nums[index])
    answer = 0
    smallest = float("inf")
    for index in range(size - 1, -1, -1):
        if prefix[index] < nums[index] < smallest:
            answer += 1
        smallest = min(smallest, nums[index])
    return answer
